newsitem.title: USA: Michigan tax cuts add up to $6.5 bln - governor.
newsitem.headline: Michigan tax cuts add up to $6.5 bln - governor.

text.p: - A spate of 21 tax cuts over the last six years in Michigan has resulted in $6.5 billion of tax reductions, Gov. John Engler said Friday.
Engler said the updated number from the state's Treasury department meant that an average family of four in Michigan has saved $2,000 in taxes.

"In Michigan, we're proud to be an example for the rest of the nation on how to lower taxes and spur the economy while balancing a budget year after year," Engler said in a press released that suggested the Wolverine State add a new nickname -- the Tax Cut State.
Among taxes that have been cut were property, single business, inheritance and income taxes.
